item.title: The one-Layer Antarctic model for Dynamical Downscaling of Ice–ocean Exchanges (LADDIE) version 2.0
item.dc:creator: Erwin Lambert, Franka Jesse, Constantijn J. Berends
item.description:
Geoscientific Model Development — matched: ice sheet, ice shelf, Antarctic, Antarctica, sea level, sea-level rise, downscaling
The future contribution of Antarctica to sea-level rise is strongly dependent on the melting of floating ice shelves by the underlying ocean. Here, we present version 2 of the two-dimensional ocean model LADDIE. We evaluate the model by comparing it to three-dimensional ocean models and satellite observations, showing good performance at low computational cost. With this open-source model, we hope to contribute to the evolution toward more realistic melting in ice sheet model simulations.

item.title: Englacial authigenesis in deep Antarctic ice: implications for Martian dust oxidation
item.dc:creator: Luca Lanci, Barbara Delmonte, Michele Mattioli, L. Valentini, Giovanni Baccolo, Paul B. Niles, … (+3)
item.description:
Communications Earth & Environment — matched: englacial, Antarctic, ice core, proxy
The discovery of englacial authigenesis has the potential to reshape our interpretation of insoluble dust records in ice cores and our understanding of planetary ice-bearing deposits on Mars. Mineralogical changes in deep ice involve iron mobilization and transformation driven by the circulation of acidic fluids within the ice matrix, leading to the authigenic formation of jarosite. Here we show that englacial authigenesis is documented across different Antarctic deep ice cores and involves the formation of mineral phases such as goethite/lepidocrocite and hematite/maghemite, in addition to jarosite. The coexistence of these phases reflects micron-scale variability in pH and water activity within the englacial brine network. Englacial authigenesis introduces biases in bulk mineralogical proxies used to reconstruct dust source conditions, and provides a grounded explanation for the anomalously high dust magnetization observed in deep Antarctic ice. We further propose that the repeated burial of dust within planetary ice reservoirs, as expected on Mars over orbital timescales, represents a viable mechanism for the oxidation, aggregation and magnetic activation of Martian airborne dust, without requiring prolonged warm and wet surface conditions. Brines generated within deep ice can provide reactive micro-environments for geochemical reactions and dust aggregation, including potentially on Mars and other planetary ice environments, according to micro-scale observations from Antarctic ice cores.

item.title: Deep waters in the Southwest Pacific do not record a release of excess respired carbon during the early deglacial CO₂ rise
item.dc:creator: Lowell Stott, Elisabeth L. Sikes
item.description:
Global and Planetary Change — matched: Southern Ocean, deglaciation, last glacial maximum, LGM, Holocene, radiocarbon, carbon cycle
During the last deglaciation, atmospheric CO 2 rose rapidly by 45 ppm during Heinrich Stadial 1 (HS1), but whether this increase was accompanied by large-scale ventilation of deep and abyssal Pacific carbon reservoirs remains uncertain. In the southwest Pacific, where mid-depth and deep Pacific waters exchange with the Southern Ocean, cores span the depths that rapid HS1 ventilation would involve. We compiled published benthic foraminiferal δ 13 C records along a depth transect spanning intermediate to lower deep waters. Holocene and Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) profiles reproduce the known vertical structure, and benthic δ 13 C increased progressively during the later stages of the LGM, several thousand years before HS1. Through HS1 itself the deep and abyssal records do not change: their trend is 0.00‰ kyr −1 (95% CI −0.06 to +0.06, n = 4 cores), and the vertical δ 13 C gradient, already relaxed before HS1 began, does not vary within it. The same holds through the Younger Dryas — the two intervals in which atmospheric CO₂ rose fastest. Benthic δ 13 C is +0.13‰ higher during HS1 than the LGM average, but measured against the two thousand years immediately preceding HS1 that offset is +0.09‰ and not distinguishable from zero. Furthermore, in the deep Pacific, radiocarbon does not record the anomalously old, isolated reservoir that rapid HS1 ventilation requires. We propose instead an open carbon budget—net glacial carbon loss with episodic deglacial return, modulated by spatially heterogeneous circulation. In this scenario, ventilation of the upper and intermediate cells during HS1 is permitted, but rapid ventilation of a deep, respired‑carbon-rich reservoir is neither required nor recorded. More broadly, these results motivate open-system frameworks for the deglacial carbon cycle—in which the ocean–atmosphere–biosphere inventory is not assumed closed—rather than a single, basin-wide Pacific ventilation event.

item.title: Reconstruction of Climate and Glaciers on Mount Elbrus in the 15th–21st Centuries Using CMIP6 Model Data
item.dc:creator: I. A. Korneva, Oleg Rybak, E. A. Dolgova, Nelly Elagina
item.description:
Izvestiya Atmospheric and Oceanic Physics — matched: glacier, paleoclimate, ice core, CMIP, climate change, SSP
— The main objective of this work is to create long-term series of air temperature and precipitation for the 15th–21st centuries to model the glaciation of Mount Elbrus. For this purpose, CMIP6 climate model data for 1466–2100 are used. Statistical comparisons of model series with different types of observations and paleoreconstructions are carried out: meteorological observations on weather stations, dendrochronological reconstructions of air temperature and precipitation, and the reconstruction of snow accumulation on the West Elbrus Plateau by ice core data. The comparison showed that the paleoclimatic model data for the 15th–19th centuries can be compared with data from paleoreconstructions on time scales more than decades. The best match with observations and reconstructions is obtained by the set of criteria over different periods of times for the INM-CM4-8 and ACCESS-ESM1-5 models. Systematic errors of the selected models are eliminated using a linear correction based on monthly average anomalies calculated from the observations at the Terskol weather station. It is shown that the amplitude of air temperature and precipitation fluctuations, as well as the mass balance calculated from these characteristics, at different time scales according to CMIP6 model data, are significantly lower than according to reconstruction data. It is found that the mass balance of the Elbrus glaciers, calculated using simple regression relationships based only on data on air temperature and precipitation in several periods of the 19th–20th centuries, does not agree with reconstruction data of glacier oscillations. The final prognostic series by the end of 2100 show an increase in air temperature by 2–6°C, depending on the climate change scenario; the amount of winter precipitation will increase from 8 to 20% depending on the scenario, and the amount of summer precipitation, on the contrary, will decrease to 20% (except for the SSP3-7.0 scenario).

item.title: Estimates of Changes in the State of the Ice Sheets of the Northern Hemisphere over the Next 100 000 Years
item.dc:creator: A. N. Ploskov, Alexey V. Eliseev, Igor I. Mokhov
item.description:
Izvestiya Atmospheric and Oceanic Physics — matched: ice sheet, stochastic forcing, sea level, CO2, reanalysis, ensemble
Abstract Ensemble simulations are performed with a modified version of the IceBern2D two-dimensional vertically isothermal ice sheets model of the Northern Hemisphere. The computation domain is limited to the Northern Hemisphere. ERA5 reanalysis data are used for the present-day state. Future atmospheric forcing is adopted from the simulations with the Climber-2.3 climate model, which is forced by the anthropogenic CO2 emissions into the atmosphere and by the changes of the parameters of the Earth orbit. In the subset of the simulations, stochastic terms with experiment-dependent decorrelation length up to 1000 are added to the abovementioned deterministic forcing. Changes in the orbital parameters over the next 100 000 years do not lead to strong glaciations in any of the simulations, and the global sea level variations are limited to several meters. This is even enforced by anthropogenically induced climate warming, because, despite anthropogenic emissions ceasing after several centuries, the climate is warmer than the preindustrial state even after 100 000 years of simulations. Stochastic forcing may lead to strong deviations in the ice sheet state trajectory from the deterministic one.

item.title: Formational Conditions of Ribbed Moraines in Norway: An Inventory and Distribution Analysis
item.dc:creator: Thomas J. Barnes, Thomas V. Schuler, Karianne S. Lilleøren, Louise S. Schmidt (16911075)
item.description:
Norwegian Journal of Geology — matched: ice sheet, subglacial, ice flow, last glacial maximum, machine learning
Ribbed moraines are common landforms in formerly glaciated areas and are indicative of subglacial conditions during the time of their formation and may, thus, provide a window into environments that are largely inaccessible also in contemporary ice sheets.However, their process of formation is disputed, as past subglacial conditions are difficult to reconstruct.In this study, we investigate formational conditions using a comprehensive ribbed moraine inventory from Norway, morphometric information, and modelled glacial and hydrological information.We first produce a high-resolution (10 m) ribbed moraine dataset for all of mainland Norway using a machine-learning algorithm.This dataset is used to identify common characteristics for ribbed moraines in nine variables: (i) morphometric (elevation, slope, and curvature), (ii) glacial (basal temperature, ice thickness, and ice velocity), and (iii) hydrological (flow accumulation, hydraulic head, and hydraulic gradient).These variables are evaluated using ice-sheet conditions at 21 ka BP taken from an ice model-based reconstruction of the European ice-sheet complex during the last glacial maximum.To balance statistical sampling, values for areas of ribbed moraines are compared to an equivalent number of samples from otherwise comparable areas where ribbed moraines are not present.Our findings show that: (a) ribbed moraines typically form in low-gradient and low-curvature areas, (b) areas with high hydraulic head, low hydraulic gradient, and slow ice flow are important for ribbed moraine formation, while factors such as elevation and ice thickness are too spatially variable to establish a large-scale link, (c) the occurrence of ribbed moraines in areas of high hydraulic head, low hydraulic gradient and low ice velocity suggests formation in transitional areas between slow and fast flowing ice, which may resemble a "patchwork" of slippery and sticky spots.While the determined relationships are robust, they do not confirm a specific formative mechanism.We therefore suggest that ribbed moraines may be one of many results from multiple processes operating under similar boundary conditions.

item.title: Temperature dependence of grain size in Tibetan ice core
item.dc:creator: Zhengqiang He, Baiqing Xu
item.description:
The Cryosphere — matched: glacier, polar, ice core, d18O, climate change
We continuously measured ice crystal sizes along two ice cores from the Tibetan Plateau. We found that the pattern of crystal size variation with depth is similar to that in polar ice cores. Crystal sizes increase abruptly in refrozen ice layers, while they decrease in impurity-rich bands. Notably, in specific layers, crystal size is linked to δ18O, which means the crystal sizes in mountain glacier ice cores can retain temperature signals, helping us understand past climate change.

item.title: Impacts of simulated coastal ocean alkalinity enhancement on the seasonal carbon cycle in European waters under a low- and a high-emission scenario
item.dc:creator: Chiara Ciscato, Neha Mehendale, Tronje P. Kemena, Sandy Avrutin, David P. Keller
item.description:
Earth System Dynamics — matched: carbon cycle, Earth system model, Earth system, CO2, emission scenario
Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) is a marine carbon dioxide removal method with large-scale potential. Using an Earth System Model, we explored the effects of continuous coastal OAE application on the seasonal carbon cycle under low and high emissions. We found that stratification retains higher alkalinity over summer, reducing the ocean pCO2 and turning the region into a year-round carbon sink. Additionally, high emissions lower the ocean’s buffering capacity and increase winter CO2 uptake.

item.title: The interface of data assimilation and machine learning
item.dc:creator: Eviatar Bach
item.description:
arXiv physics.ao-ph — matched: data assimilation, machine learning
arXiv:2610.07496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data assimilation (DA) is the process of combining forecasts from a model with observations in order to optimally estimate the state of a system. This is critical for chaotic systems, such as the atmosphere, since if observations are not continually assimilated the model will quickly lose skill. DA is routinely performed (usually every 6 hours) at operational forecasting centres around the world. In this article we discuss the interface of machine learning (ML) and DA. This is still an emerging and quickly developing field, and this article tries to give an overview of some of the main topics and methods.

item.title: Rock glaciers in the Hindu Kush Himalaya: A regional synthesis
item.dc:creator: Prashant Baral, Mohd Farooq Azam, Sonam Wangchuk, Gh Jeelani, Suraj Mal, Ashok Priyadarshan Dimri
item.description:
Arctic Antarctic and Alpine Research — matched: glacier, permafrost, machine learning, remote sensing
Rock glaciers are cryospheric landforms in high-mountain regions and indicators of permafrost occurrence and change under accelerating climate warming. This review synthesizes 67 peer-reviewed studies on rock glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH) published between 1970 and 2024 to assess the research landscape. Publications increased after 2016, with growth after 2020 and a peak in 2024. Large-scale inventories published through 2024 contain more than 61,000 mapped rock glacier records within the HKH boundary but differ in mapping framework and remain spatially incomplete. In the Himalayan subregion, an upscaled first-order assessment estimated approximately 3,747 km2 of rock glacier area and a water volume equivalent of 51.80 ± 10.36 km3. Although substantially less than glacier storage at the Himalayan scale, local model-based studies indicate that rock glacier storage may be comparable to, or exceed, glacier storage in some semi-arid subregions. Earlier studies focused on geomorphological mapping and permafrost assessment, whereas recent research increasingly integrates remote sensing, geophysics, machine learning, and hydrological modeling. Rock glaciers can contribute to sustaining streamflow and supporting livelihoods, while changes in their condition can influence permafrost-related hazards. Nevertheless, HKH rock glaciers remain incompletely inventoried, with uncertainties and limited hydrological understanding, requiring interdisciplinary research into climate–rock glacier interactions.

item.title: Spatiotemporal evolution of the Zhacang paleolake system at Central Qinghai–Xizang Plateau and its implication for boron and lithium enrichment
item.dc:creator: Huibin Zhao, 卫良 苗, Chang Huang, Pin Gao, Xiaochen Ma, Yulong Li, … (+4)
item.description:
CATENA — matched: meltwater, Holocene, permafrost, remote sensing
Numerous salt lakes on the Qinghai–Xizang Plateau (QXP) host significant boron (B) and lithium (Li) brine deposits. Understanding their spatiotemporal evolution is essential for clarifying the mechanisms of B–Li enrichment. This study reconstructs the spatiotemporal evolution of the Zhacang paleolake system in the central QXP for the first time by integrating remote sensing imagery, field geomorphological observations, optically stimulated luminescence dating, and X–ray diffraction. Results indicate that the paleolake system experienced lake–level highstands at 12.62–12.20 ka and ∼ 7.33 ka, followed by progressive contraction and fragmentation since the middle Holocene, against which abrupt fluctuations at ∼9.11 ka, 4.24 ka, 2.01 ka, and 0.80 ka were superimposed. Variations in Indian Summer Monsoon precipitation, glacial meltwater and permafrost thaw appear to have been the primary hydrological controls on paleolake fluctuations, while the system also responded to abrupt climate events on centennial–to–millennial timescales. In addition, under a similar regional climatic background, B and Li brine deposits were identified primarily in Zhacang Chaka and Nier Co. This heterogeneity was primarily controlled by sustained proximal hydrothermal recharge and enhanced by the chemical weathering of B and Li rich magmatic rocks in the Xiongba Basin. Meanwhile, the Zhacang Chaka promoted the capture and concentration of solutes from the entire paleolake catchment as the terminal lake, further amplifying B and Li enrichment. Overall, this study advances understanding of the spatiotemporal evolution of B and Li enriched salt lakes on the QXP and the heterogeneous enrichment of sub-lakes within the paleolake system.

item.title: Quadrupolar sea level fluctuations reveal episodes of rapid polar wander
item.dc:creator: Mathew Domeier, Leandro Cesar Gallo, Chloé M. Marcilly, Trond Helge Torsvik
item.description:
Science — matched: polar, sea level
True polar wander (TPW) is presently occurring at a rate of ~10 centimeters per year, exceeding the mean rate of differential plate motion. Whether this rate is transient and negligible on geological timescales or whether Earth has experienced rapid TPW lasting millions of years is unclear. Paleomagnetic evidence has been used to propose fast episodes of TPW, but limitations of the paleomagnetic record have precluded definitive results. Rapid TPW will induce global sea level fluctuations associated with relative changes in centrifugal potential, offering an independent test. We evaluated this prediction using continental flooding reconstructions and identified multiple robust quadrupolar patterns since 320 million years ago, confirming that protracted rapid TPW has occurred on Earth and that couplings among Earth's rotational dynamics, mantle processes, and surface environments can be strongly episodic.

item.title: The Dynamics of Anthropogenic Snow Patch Melting and Assessment of Pollution in Meltwater
item.dc:creator: Valentina A. Lobkina, A. A. Muzychenko
item.description:
Water Resources — matched: meltwater, remote sensing
Abstract Annually, more than 1500 × 103 m3 of snow are collected and transported from Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk territory. This volume of snow is stored at two sites, where it melts naturally over the warm seasons. The resultant meltwater flows unregulated into the urban environment. As a consequence, flooding of urban infrastructure objects and increased environmental stress across the city’s territory ensue. This work presents actual volumes of melting recorded for the period 2018–2022, combining remote sensing techniques and ground-based measurements. These observed volumes are compared against results simulated using four different methods, among which the ETI model proved most effective, yielding the smallest error relative to actual annual snowmelt volumes. Additionally, an empirical snowmelt model based on observational data is proposed, offering potential utility for flood risk assessment and contaminant transport modeling. In 2018 and 2019, meltwater samples were collected at the beginning and end of the snowmelt period from snow storage sites. Heavy metal content (V, Cr, Cu, Zn, Cd, Pb) was measured in these samples. The highest concentrations were found at the onset of the snowmelt period (June), declining noticeably toward its conclusion (August). Using calculated snowmelt volumes and pollutant concentrations, the mass load of pollutants was assessed. A significant imbalance in major cations and anions typical of natural waters was detected in the snow storage sites meltwater, characterized by elevated levels of chloride ions (Cl–) and sodium ions (Na+). This indicates substantial impact from anti-skid agents used throughout the city, which accumulate on snow storage sites following snow removal operations.

item.title: Tropical Indo-Pacific intermediate waters remain in a Little Ice Age cold state
item.dc:creator: Xuefei Chen, Kaiwen Ta, Xuefeng Wang, Deng Wenfeng, 韦刚健, Xiaotong Peng, … (+1)
item.description:
Geology — matched: proxy, Earth system model, Earth system, ensemble
Model simulations predict that the deep Pacific Ocean still harbors cooling from the Little Ice Age (LIA; ca. 1450 to 1850 CE), implying vast unrealized heat uptake. Yet proxy records capable of testing this prediction at intermediate depths over the past millennium remain scarce across the Pacific. We address this gap using Li/Mg thermometry on a living cold-water coral from 1345 m in the South China Sea, with U-Th dating confirming continuous growth from the Medieval Climate Anomaly (MCA; ca. 850 to 1250 CE) to present. Li/Mg data reveal a cooling of 1.0 ± 0.2 °C from the MCA to the LIA, with the trend persisting at a reduced rate into the early Current Warm Period (ca. 1850 CE to present) and no recovery to MCA levels, a pattern also captured by Community Earth System Model (CESM) Last Millennium Ensemble simulations. In contrast, sea-surface temperatures have recovered from LIA levels, revealing a pronounced vertical thermal decoupling. These results demonstrate that deeper intermediate waters beneath the Indo-Pacific Warm Pool remain in a LIA cold state, implying that the ocean interior’s heat uptake capacity is far from exhausted and that recent increases in intermediate-depth heat content likely mark the onset of a protracted equilibration process rather than the approach to a new steady state.

item.title: Evaluating sediment color as a paleoceanographic proxy in Santos Basin continental slope sediments, SW Atlantic
item.dc:creator: Michel Michaelovitch de Mahiques, Marco Aurélio Guedes Pereira, Leonardo Scherer Severo, Paulo Alves de Lima Ferreira, Rodrigo Baptista de Barros, Samara Cazzoli y Goya, … (+5)
item.description:
Geo-Marine Letters — matched: proxy, sediment core, radiocarbon
Abstract Sediment color is a valuable proxy in paleoceanography, reflecting chemical and mineralogical composition influenced by biogeochemical processes and depositional environments. This study investigates the relationship between sediment color (RGB and CIE L*a*b*) and metals in three radiocarbon-dated sediment cores from the Santos Basin continental slope (SW Atlantic). The cores, located within the Upper Circumpolar Water domain, span different time intervals. Results show significant color variation, especially after the Bølling–Allerød event. Although we identified statistical correlations between metals and color parameters (e.g., positive for Ca, negative for Ti), multiple regression analyses indicated that, among the major constituents of these sediments, calcium content was the strongest statistical predictor of color variability across the cores. The statistical association between metals and color was not consistently robust, particularly with significant changes before and after the Bølling-Allerød transition, possibly due to early diagenetic processes. We argue that the relationship between sediment color and composition in samples from the Santos Basin is more complex than simple correlation coefficients, as observed at other continental margins.

item.title: Multi-model ocean oxygen fields predicted by conditional diffusion models
item.dc:creator: Linus Vogt, Laure Zanna
item.description:
arXiv physics.ao-ph — matched: Earth system model, Earth system, ensemble
arXiv:2610.08523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dissolved oxygen is important for the ocean's ecosystems and biogeochemical cycles. Yet, Earth System Models (ESMs) vary in their simulations of the present-day and future ocean oxygen inventory. To narrow down the uncertainty in estimates of ocean oxygen content, we train a conditional generative diffusion model on outputs of a multi-model ESM ensemble to learn the conditional distribution of upper-ocean oxygen given physical input variables such as temperature and salinity. This generative model has considerable skill in the Atlantic and Southern Oceans, and can generate realistic oxygen samples under conditions not seen in the training data. We validate this model using observational datasets, and use it to generate oxygen fields for models without oxygen data using only temperature and salinity as conditioning inputs. This physics-conditioned extrapolation suggests that model biases in the tropical Pacific Oxygen Minimum Zone may be smaller than currently assumed when considering a larger set of physical ocean states. Our approach provides a complementary way to represent probabilistic multi-model climate distributions.

item.title: From pollen to pixels: Towards spatially meaningful pollen-based vegetation reconstructions across southeastern Australia
item.dc:creator: Alastair Wills, Annika Herbert, Janelle Stevenson, Martin Theuerkauf, Haidee Cadd, Simon Connor, … (+7)
item.description:
The Holocene — matched: Holocene, downscaling
Reconstruction of past vegetation underpins understanding of long-term ecosystem and societal change, helping to contextualise present-day patterns in biodiversity, ecosystem trajectories and effective landscape management practices against historical ecosystem states. This is particularly important in regions, such as southeastern Australia, where landscapes have been extensively shaped by long-term human activity including Indigenous fire management, creating cultural landscapes that can be difficult to identify through traditional palaeoecological techniques. Quantitative vegetation reconstruction models provide an opportunity to reconstruct these systems with greater precision but require robust validation with real-world data before application to past landscapes. Here, we present the first Southern Hemisphere application of the Extended Downscaling Approach (EDA), focussing on western Tasmania and southeastern Victoria. Using 86 modern pollen samples from moss and sedimentary records across seven study locations, we test whether the EDA reconstructs local-scale vegetation cover more accurately than uncorrected pollen percentages. By comparing EDA outputs with ground-surveyed vegetation cover, we find that the EDA reduces taxonomic representation biases, particularly for tree taxa. Across all study locations, EDA reconstructions differ from surveyed vegetation by <2.5% on average, compared with 4–9% for uncorrected pollen, while also showing higher Bray-Curtis similarity and Squared Chord Distance (SCD) values consistently below southeastern Australian analogue benchmarks. While this study does not assess the spatial outputs of the EDA, it demonstrates that the model can provide reliable local-scale vegetation reconstructions, supporting future spatial validation and Holocene applications within ancient cultural landscapes.

item.title: ДИНАМИКА БИОРАЗНООБРАЗИЯ ВЫСОТНЫХ ПОЯСОВ В ГУМИДНОМ КЛИМАТЕ САЯН: ПАЛЕОГРАФИЧЕСКИЕ РЕКОНСТРУКЦИИ
item.dc:creator: А.Д. КОШКАРОВ, В.Л. КОШКАРОВА, Д.И. НАЗИМОВА
item.description:
География и природные ресурсы — matched: Holocene, radiocarbon, climate change
На основе палеокарпологических данных (макроостатки голоценовых растений), имеющих радиоуглеродное подтверждение по 14С, выполнена реконструкция лесного покрова на горном профиле северного макросклона Западного Саяна по временным отрезкам, характеризуемым определенными климатическими режимами с начала среднего голоцена и до современного периода (7898 календарных лет). В ходе исследований разработан усовершенствованный метод анализа палеокарпологического материала, позволяющий дать интерпретацию состава растительных сообществ прошлого на локальном и высотно-поясном масштабных уровнях. Установлена динамика трансформаций структуры зональных типов растительности и высотно-поясных комплексов типов леса, обусловленная циклами климатических изменений, а также влиянием антропогенного воздействия на последних этапах голоцена. Для каждого временного периода построены схемы распределения господствующих лесных формаций в разных высотных поясах - от подтайги и лесостепи до горной темнохвойной тайги и субальпийских редколесий и тундр. Их диагностика основывалось не только на преобладании ископаемых макроостатков тех или иных лесообразователей, но и на видовом составе разных эколого-ценотических групп растений травяно-кустарничкового яруса. Особое внимание уделялось участию в ископаемых комплексах представителей поясно-зональных групп. Research Center “Krasnoyarsk Scientific Center, Siberian Branch, Russian Academy of Sciences”, Krasnoyarsk, Russia Based on paleocarpological data (macrofossils of Holocene plants) confirmed by 14C radiocarbon dating, a reconstruction of forest cover on a mountain profile of the northern macroslope of the Western Sayan was performed for time periods characterized by specific climatic regimes from the beginning of the Middle Holocene to the present day (7898 calendar years). The study resulted in the development of an improved method for analyzing paleocarpological material, which makes it possible to interpret the composition of plant communities of the past at local and altitudinal-zonal scale levels. The dynamics of transformations in the structure of zonal vegetation types and altitudinal complexes of forest types, conditioned by the cycles of climate change and the influence of anthropogenic impacts during the last stages of the Holocene, has been revealed. For each time period, distribution patterns of dominant forest formations in different altitudinal zones were constructed - from subtaiga and forest-steppe to mountain dark coniferous taiga and subalpine sparse forests and tundra. Their identification was based not only on the predominance of macrofossils of certain forest-forming plants, but also on the species composition of various ecological-cenotic groups of plants of the herbaceous-dwarf shrub layer. Particular attention was paid to the participation of representatives of belt-zonal groups in the fossil complexes.

item.title: Xaurora: Generative Weather Forecasting with Denoising Stochastic Interpolants from a Foundation Model Prior
item.dc:creator: Eliot Walt, Miltiadis Kofinas, Nikolaj M\"ucke, Efstratios Gavves, Dim Coumou
item.description:
arXiv physics.ao-ph — matched: uncertainty quantification, ensemble
arXiv:2610.06509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep learning has revolutionised weather forecasting in recent years, especially through atmospheric foundation models, which offer competitive skill for a fraction of the computational costs of classic physics-based models. However, most existing foundation models are deterministic, limiting the generation of large ensembles for accurate uncertainty quantification, extreme weather risk assessment, and long-range weather forecasting. Furthermore, these models incur a large, often prohibitive, computational overhead to train from scratch. To address these shortcomings, we turn a pretrained deterministic prior model, namely the Aurora foundation model, into a generative ensemble-prediction model. To that end, we introduce a novel generative method, Denoising Stochastic Interpolants, combined with a replay buffer for Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) rollout, enabling probabilistic training of SDE trajectories. Our stochastic foundation model, Xaurora, is finetuned from the small Aurora version, yet it approaches the state-of-the-art on global ensemble metrics and is competitive with the large version of Aurora. Our method is parameter and sample efficient, and generates skilful 15-day forecasts in 13 minutes. Our results demonstrate that deterministic foundation models can be efficiently extended into even stronger stochastic models.

item.title: Role of the Foehn Effect in Glacier Melting in Grønfjorden (Spitsbergen): Case Study of August 4–5, 2025
item.dc:creator: А. А. Шестакова, Alexandra Narizhnaya, Irina Repina, Artem Pashkin, A.Yu. Artamonov, A. E. Mamontov, … (+1)
item.description:
Izvestiya Atmospheric and Oceanic Physics — matched: glacier
Abstract This study examines the influence of the foehn effect on a heat budget of glaciers in Grønfjorden on Spitsbergen. Observations on the Vestre Grønfjordbreen (West Grønfjord Glacier) reveal a sharp increase in the turbulent flux of sensible heat during a foehn occurring on August 4–5, 2025. According to calculations using aerodynamic formulas, the foehn also increases the flux of a latent heat. As a result, the total contribution of the turbulent heat exchange is several times larger than the contribution of the radiation balance. The estimated ice melting rate reaches 11 mm/h, while the calculated melting layer is equal to 10.6 cm per day with the foehn. In addition, to study the effect of mesoscale circulations, the results of high-resolution (400 m) numerical modeling of the atmosphere are used, and these are in a good agreement with the measured melting layer on a scale of several days. The simulation results show that, among the surrounding glaciers, the Austre Grønfjordbreen (East Grønfjord Glacier) is the most susceptible to melting under the influence of a foehn.

item.title: LIPOTHERM: A Calibration Framework for GDGT Paleothermometry Based on Machine Learning
item.dc:creator: Vikash Kumar, Manish Tiwari, Biswajit Roy
item.description:
Geochemistry Geophysics Geosystems — matched: machine learning
Abstract SST reconstruction from glycerol dialkyl glycerol tetraethers (GDGT) preserved in marine sediments is an important tool in quantitative paleoclimatology. These reconstructions require calibration frameworks that provide mapping between sediment GDGT data and temperature values. Improvements in modeling and data coverage can reduce bias in existing calibrations, such as those based on the univariate TEX 86 index and other multivariate frameworks. GDGT cyclization is also known to be affected by nutrient stress as a non‐thermal control. In this study, we present LIPOTHERM (Lipid Paleothermometry), a new GDGT‐SST calibration trained on an extensive collection of globally distributed core‐top GDGT data using supervised machine learning. LIPOTHERM features substantially lower calibration root mean square error than existing forms. Inclusion of core‐top nutrient conditions as auxiliary predictors further lowers the calibration error. LIPOTHERM demonstrates that robust paleothermometry frameworks can be constructed by accumulating incremental improvements over different methodological refinements involving algorithm selection, feature space representation, expanding data coverage, and adding auxiliary non‐thermal covariates.

item.title: Mechanisms and patterns of snow depth and land surface temperature interactions in arid mountains: coupling coordination and lagged responses across Xinjiang, China
item.dc:creator: Haixing Li, Xiaolong Bao, Shiqi Lu, Yi Chu, Jun Lu, Mengge Xiao, … (+1)
item.description:
The Cryosphere
Mountain snow is a critical water source, but its warming response is complex. This study developed a new method to examine this in arid Xinjiang mountains using long-term satellite data, revealing a three-level control system and that a strong snow-temperature link does not guarantee a healthy system; it also provides a framework for water availability prediction and climate adaptation.

item.title: Benchmarking a new urban scheme in the ORCHIDEE 2.2 land surface model
item.dc:creator: Morgane Lalonde, Sophie Bastin, Ludovic Oudin, Pedro Felipe Arboleda-Obando, Agnès Ducharne
item.description:
Geoscientific Model Development
Some climate models still represent cities as if they were natural ground. For one of these models, we built a new way to represent cities. The update includes how reflective surfaces are, building height, stored heat, and how much ground is sealed. The novelty is to treat sealed ground not only at the surface, but also below it. Tested at twenty urban sites, the new version better represents exchanges of energy between the ground and the air, supporting more reliable urban climate studies.

item.title: Virtual Rain v1.0: a unified toolkit for high-resolution rainfall simulation and disaggregation
item.dc:creator: Francesco Cappelli, Salvatore Grimaldi, Andrea Petroselli, Emanuele Santinami
item.description:
Geoscientific Model Development
Rainfall information is essential for flood studies and water management, but detailed records are often unavailable. We developed Virtual Rain, an open toolkit that generates realistic rainfall series and converts daily rainfall data into finer time scales. Using commonly available rainfall records and information on rainfall extremes, the tool reproduces key rainfall characteristics with good accuracy. It is freely available through open-source software and an interactive web platform.
